audit_findings.title: Security identifier does not match the valued company
audit_findings.mechanism: The security mapping controls which market price, filings, earnings, and share count are combined in the per-share valuation.
audit_findings.evidence: Our common stock is quoted on The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC under the trading symbol “SCVL.”
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrably identify Shoe Carnival as SCVL, while the valuation is labeled SHOE. Whether SHOE is an intentional internal alias remains unresolved. If it is not, the displayed price and resulting investment conclusion may concern a different security, invalidating the valuation rather than merely shifting it by a limited amount.
audit_findings.action: Verify the identifier master and document that SHOE resolves to SCVL; then confirm the $14.07 price, all filings, the 28.202121 million diluted shares, and final outputs refer to Shoe Carnival, Inc.

audit_findings.title: The bridge assumes every dollar of cash and securities is distributable
audit_findings.mechanism: Any operating cash incorrectly treated as excess is added dollar-for-dollar through the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our primary uses of cash are normally for working capital, which are principally inventory purchases, investments in our stores, such as rebanners and new stores, remodels and relocations, distribution center initiatives, lease payments associated with our real estate leases, potential dividend payments, potential share repurchases under our share repurchase program and the financing of capital projects, including investments in new systems.
audit_findings.explanation: The distributable amount is unresolved, but the issue is bounded by the entire $129.348 million bridge addition. Removing all of it would reduce base value from $40.90 to about $36.31 per share and the 30% buy-below level from $28.63 to about $25.42, still well above the supplied $14.07 price. Thus this finding alone cannot change the stated valuation conclusion, although it can materially affect the reported value estimate.
audit_findings.action: Calculate excess cash using seasonal low balances, inventory funding needs, lease and capital commitments, and revolver restrictions; rerun the bridge with only the supported excess amount.

audit_findings.title: Deferred-compensation assets may be added without the matching liability
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge includes the $13.248 million marketable-securities asset but does not offset the matching current and long-term deferred-compensation liabilities; only the $0.360 million net surplus belongs in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: These Marketable Securities are designed to mitigate volatility in our Consolidated Statements of Income associated with our non-qualified deferred compensation plan.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q demonstrates the mismatch: deferred-compensation liabilities were $12.888 million against $13.248 million of related securities. Correcting it would reduce base equity value by about 1.1%, from $40.90 to approximately $40.44 per share, which is too small to change the conclusion relative to the supplied $14.07 price.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the bridge by subtracting the filed $12.888 million liability, equivalently adding only the $0.360 million net surplus, and confirm the securities are not duplicated elsewhere.

audit_findings.title: Immediate growth paths may miss disclosed margin normalization
audit_findings.magnitude: $10–$15 million disclosed Fiscal 2026 rebanner impact and a filed 120-basis-point first-quarter gross-margin decline; total valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Lower near-term margins reduce owner earnings below the $72.9 million anchor and alter the growth path and operating present value; persistent pressure would also reduce terminal earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The promotional activity necessary to sell this inventory is expected to reduce gross profit margins in Fiscal 2026 compared to the 36.6% gross profit margin achieved in Fiscal 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is more than a generic risk: the company forecast lower Fiscal 2026 margins, and first-quarter gross margin actually declined from 34.5% to 33.3%. The disclosed $10–$15 million operating-income impact is 14%–21% of the $72.9 million OE anchor before considering tax and OE adjustments. Because every scenario starts at flat or positive growth and roughly half of operating value is terminal value, an unmodeled normalization period is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion. The record does not show how much of this pressure is already embedded in the latest-actual anchor.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $72.9 million anchor to the latest trailing results, separate one-time CEO and strategic-review charges, and rerun each scenario with an explicit Fiscal 2026–2027 bridge for markdowns, tariffs, rebanner costs, store closures, and any later normalization.

audit_findings.title: Terminal durability depends heavily on three uncontracted suppliers
audit_findings.magnitude: 46% of Fiscal 2025 sales; terminal value is 47.7%–51.5% of operating value
audit_findings.mechanism: A supplier loss or allocation reduction would lower durable OE and potentially invalidate the terminal growth and margin assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: Three branded suppliers, Nike, Skechers and Crocs, collectively accounted for approximately 46 % of our Net Sales in Fiscal 2025, 48 % of our Net Sales in Fiscal 2024 and 45 % of our Net Sales in Fiscal 2023.
audit_findings.explanation: The concentration and absence of long-term contracts are demonstrated, but no supplier loss or allocation reduction is presently reported and no earnings impact can be established. It is therefore a forward-looking durability risk rather than a current valuation error. Its importance is elevated because nearly half of sales involve the three suppliers and approximately half of operating value comes from terminal value.
audit_findings.action: Monitor supplier disclosures and allocation trends, and prepare separate OE stresses for reduced or lost Nike, Skechers, and Crocs sales, including lost vendor support, substitution margins, and working-capital effects.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition contingent consideration is a non-debt claim on equity cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.459 million filed fair-value liability, approximately $0.02 per share; contractual maximum $5.0 million, approximately $0.18 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The contingent payment is a claim on equity cash that should be deducted in the bridge unless its expected cost is already captured without double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: Additional consideration of up to $ 5.0 million may be paid by the Company subject to the achievement of three-year growth targets.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q demonstrates a $0.459 million liability. Deducting it would reduce base equity value by about 0.04%. Even the $5.0 million contractual maximum is only about 0.43% of the $1.154 billion base equity value and would not change the conclusion relative to the supplied price.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the latest $0.459 million fair-value liability in the bridge, verify its balance at the valuation date, and ensure any future remeasurement retained in OE is not also deducted as a duplicate cost.
